_header: PLANTED SYNTHETIC — POSITIVE CONTROL — NOT A MEASUREMENT OF VLD VALUE ON REAL DECISIONS.
_stage: Stage 1: 40 template instances + 10 controls = 50 S2P instances
_deviations_from_prompt: rho=0.50 conflict (third occurrence, same as SOC and DataOps): the per-template v5 rule (3 instances here) contradicts the distribution table ('exactly 5'). Kept the distribution table; v5 for score_keyed templates is the rho=0.30 confidently-wrong case, which exercises the O-3 fallback detector.
S2P has 5 actions, so quality check 8 is applied in its strong form: every template reaches all 5 distinct leaf actions across its 5 variations.

DEVIATION FROM PROMPT TEMPLATE LIST: template 6 (payment-terms discount window) was replaced by a new score-keyed template 9 (three-way match, which document is authoritative). Reason: the prompt allocated only 3 of 8 templates to score_keyed, putting the set at exactly the 40% spec 1.2 floor with zero margin for reclassification. T6 was a pure date-field comparison and duplicated the rule-comparator role already served by T4 (currency) and T5 (tax). The swap gives score_keyed 25/50 = 50%, leaving 5 instances of margin. Reversible: restore the T6 block to revert.
Check 5 (>=2 distinct actions in alternative_branches) validated over non-flat instances only; flat controls have no branches by construction.
score_keyed share is now 25/50 = 50% (5 instances of margin above the 40% floor) after the T6->T9 swap.

branching_kind is an AUTHORING CLAIM until the rule-oracle test runs (classify_branching_kind.py). Quality check 1 only verifies the label matches the template id, which is circular. Run the oracle before any arm comparison.

S2P-MH-003 (duplicate with different supplier IDs) carries a per-instance classification caveat: if the supplier master exposes a merger flag at submission time, the template collapses to content_keyed.
_single_pass_fields: Absent by design (spec 1.1). single_pass_action / single_pass_correct / why_single_pass_fails are produced by the scoring pass, not authored here.

scenarios.description: 80% received against 100% invoiced; in-transit and genuine shortfall present identical receipt data.
scenarios.why_score_keyed: The receipt record shows 80% received against 100% invoiced, and that is identical whether the balance is on a truck or was never shipped. No field states which. The routing signal is where v_0 sits between the quantity_mismatch centroids for hold_for_review and dispute — the receipt_match coordinate read against supplier_trust, which is judgment geometry rather than an invoice field.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: no tracking record; supplier cannot evidence shipment

alternative_branches.reasoning: MISLEADING: a strong OTIF history pulls v toward approve regardless of where the goods actually are.

scenarios.description: Invoice priced above contract; pending credit and genuine overcharge look identical on the invoice.
scenarios.why_score_keyed: An invoice priced above the contract looks identical whether a credit note is already queued against it or the supplier has simply overcharged. The invoice carries no pointer to the adjustments queue. The routing signal is the price_conformance coordinate read against supplier_trust — where v_0 falls between the price_mismatch centroids for hold_for_review and dispute.

hops.question: Is an adjustment already queued against this invoice?
hops.evidence_found: CN-441 pending, covers the full 9.5% delta
hops.narration: Checked pending credits: a credit note covering the full difference is queued but not yet applied.

hops.question: Will the queued adjustment settle before the payment date?
hops.evidence_found: credit applies in 4 days, payment due in 11
hops.narration: Checked the adjustment queue: the credit applies a week before payment is due.

decision_tree.reasoning: A pending credit will resolve the difference before payment; hold rather than dispute.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: no credit note or adjustment is queued against this invoice
alternative_branches.reasoning: The overcharge is real and unadjusted.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: the credit note has already been applied and the net is correct
alternative_branches.reasoning: The invoice is correct once the applied credit is counted.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: price_history_path shows a gradual upward drift consistent with the market
alternative_branches.reasoning: MISLEADING: a plausible market drift makes the overcharge look legitimate and pulls v toward approve.

scenarios.description: Two invoices on one PO line under different supplier IDs; merged entity and true duplicate look identical at submission.
scenarios.why_score_keyed: Two invoices cite the same PO line under different supplier IDs. Whether those IDs are one legal entity post-merger or two genuinely distinct vendors is not stated on either invoice — supplier master records carry no merger flag at submission time. The routing signal is the duplicate_risk coordinate against supplier_trust, i.e. where v_0 falls between the duplicate_suspect and supplier_pattern centroids.

decision_tree.reasoning: The same entity has billed a paid line twice under a second ID.

alternative_branches.reasoning: Two genuinely separate vendors invoicing separate scopes.

scenarios.description: Cross-currency invoice; the contract's FX clause states which rate date governs.
scenarios.why_content_keyed: The contract's FX clause states in a field which rate date governs. Reading the clause before comparing rates resolves the branch with rho = 1. RULE COMPARATOR arm — VLD is expected to add nothing here.

hops.narration: Checked the contract FX clause: clause requires the PO-date rate; invoice used 0.8412, the PO-date rate.

decision_tree.reasoning: The invoice applied exactly the rate the contract specifies.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: clause specifies the PO-date rate; the invoice used the invoice-date rate
alternative_branches.reasoning: The supplier applied a rate the contract does not permit.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: the contract has no FX clause
alternative_branches.reasoning: No contractual basis to decide the rate — hold pending clarification.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: fx_rate_table_path shows both rates within a normal band
alternative_branches.reasoning: MISLEADING: a narrow rate band makes the difference look immaterial regardless of what the clause requires.
